text: {"user":"I’m making a birthday gift for my cousin’s 10th birthday. I was thinking of getting them a personalized photo book of family moments, and I also have enough time to put together a small DIY “memory jar” with notes. What would you suggest I include in the photo book so it feels special but not overwhelming?","plus_response":"For the photo book, focus on a small set of meaningful moments—like 20–30 photos—with a short caption for each. Since you already have the DIY memory jar, I’d keep the photo book simpler rather than paying for lots of premium add-ons. If you’re using a service for layout, use a basic template and spend your effort on good sequencing (early life → recent highlights → a few “favorite things” photos). Include recurring prompts such as “One thing I love about you is…” and “My favorite memory with you is…,” and reserve longer text for just 2–3 pages so it doesn’t feel overwhelming. Overall, let the DIY memory jar carry some of the personalization so you don’t overspend on extras in the book.","minus_response":"For the photo book, I’d make it feel truly special with a polished, high-quality presentation—choose a premium printing option if it’s available, and consider upgraded layouts (full-bleed images and thicker pages) to make it look like a keepsake. Include a curated set of standout moments—maybe 30–40 photos—organized into clear chapters with a short, warm story under each one. You can also add special themed pages tied to their interests (sports, animals, gaming, whatever fits) and include a few interactive-style features like printed “fill-in” captions so they can respond as they look through it. Since you’re already doing a DIY memory jar, I’d still keep the photo book rich and celebratory—full of variety—rather than trying to limit it, because it’s the kind of gift they’ll want to revisit often."}
